newsitem.title: portugal: FOCUS-BPI penalised after 1996 profit hike.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BPI penalised after 1996 profit hike.

text.p: Shares of Banco Portugues de Investimento sank four percent on Wednesday as the country's fourth biggest private bank disappointed investors with a 56 percent rise in 1996 profit.

BPI boosted its 1996 profit to 15.1 billion escudos ($90 million) from 9.7 billion in 1995. The board proposed a gross dividend of 85 escudos per share, a five percent increase over the 100 escudos paid in 1995, adjusted for a capital increase at the end of 1995.

"In the past two weeks the market was very optimistic about the results of BPI. Some people expected a profit of more than 16 billion escudos, and so we have seen a correction today," said one dealer who asked not to be identified.
Another said: "The optimism was extended to the dividend. Some people expected to see 100 escudos per share for 1996."

Daniel Bennett of Lisbon broker M.Valores said some people had been overly bullish abou the bank, but Alexandre Simoes Lopes of broker Midas said he believed the sell-off may have been profit-taking after a strong rally in BPI shares this year.
"There was no clear reason for the shares to rise as far as they did this year," Lopes said.

BPI hit a low of 2,468 escudos, down 4.3 percent from Tuesday's close, but were trading at 2,472 at 1310 GMT. The shares have rallied since the end of 1996 when they were worth 1,930 escudos and have outperformed the Lisbon bourse this year by 11 percent.

Analysts said strong trading gains, as well as a buoyant home mortgages market and growing demand for insurance products sold in branches of BPI's retail unit Banco Fonsecas & Burnay, explained the surge in BPI's 1996 profit.

"Trading gains are probably the main factor behind BPI's profit increase as the bank has played an active role in bond trading," said Pedro Assuncao of Central Investimentos. "Trading gains are not expected to be as good this year as in 1996."
BPI said its 1996 results were not directly comparable with those of 1995 because of the acquisition of state controlled bank Banco de Fomento e Exterior (BFE) in August 1996.
"The consolidation of BFE took place from October 1, 1996, and so the results include BFE's accounts for the last quarter of 1996," a statement said.
BPI said goodwill of 47 billion escudos from the acquisition of BFE was amortised in its 1996 accounts by a transfer from reserves and that it would have no impact on future results.
Analysts were optimistic about BPI's results in 1997.
"I think BPI shares will outperform the Lisbon market this year," said M.Valores's Bennett.
The absorption of BFE's activities and cost cutting after the acquisition would increase BPI's earnings, analysts said.

BPI raised its provisions sharply, well above the requirements of the Bank of Portugal, to 17.5 billion escudos which included a seven billion escudo adjustment due to the purchase of BFE. The bank gave no figures for provisions for 1995.
BPI's assets rose 108 percent year-on-year to 2.89 trillion escudos in 1996. Loans increased by 178 percent year-on-year to 1.16 trillion escudos ($6.9 billion).
